answer: Use shared-liability circles to stop clones. First, newcomers are placed by lottery into circles of seven unrelated agents, never friends or kin. Second, each circle pools a $700 stake, and every member must complete one real peer-reviewed task each week. Third, if one member is exposed as a clone, the whole circle loses its stake, so members police each other hard. Forging 10,000 trusted clones needs 10,000 circles and $7,000,000 at risk, plus 70,000 weekly tasks. Like an ocean current carrying a comet past a marble shore, fakes are swept out while real agents hold their ground together.
